_comment: LABELLED PROMPT SET for the GLiNER2 domain-discernment spike. Committed BEFORE any model runs. Each record: {id, domain, tier, text}. TIER IS THE EXPERIMENT: 'obvious' prompts contain the domain's giveaway vocabulary; 'oblique' prompts describe the SAME work without it. A model that only scores on 'obvious' is a keyword matcher, and we would implement that in 50 lines without a 1.9GB dependency. Written by Claude, so these carry the author's own tells -- synthetic accuracy is an UPPER BOUND, never a prediction for real prompts.

Draft a mutual action plan to send the champion after a successful technical evaluation.

Review this MSA and flag any indemnification clauses that are broader than our standard terms.

What notice period do we owe under this lease if we want to exit early?
Compare the IP assignment language in this contractor agreement against our employee template.
Go through this agreement and tell me where we'd be on the hook for more than we usually accept.
We're about to talk to a supplier about something confidential. Write the document both sides sign first, two years, Delaware.
Across these five agreements, when can each side walk away and what rolls over automatically if nobody says anything?
Change this so the most we could ever owe them is what they've paid us in the last year.

Review this chart note for documentation gaps that would affect the E/M level billed.
Turn these notes from when they left the ward into a short list of what's currently wrong with them and what they're taking for it.

Take these written descriptions of what's wrong with each person and match them to the standard codes, flagging anything unclear.
Write what someone should do at home after keyhole knee surgery, in plain language a child could follow.

Write a migration that adds a partial index on (org_id, created_at) where deleted_at is null.
The test passes locally and fails in CI. Diff the environments and tell me what's different.
Add retry with exponential backoff to this HTTP client, but only for idempotent methods.
Profile this endpoint — p99 went from 80ms to 1.2s after the last deploy.
Review this pull request for race conditions in the cache invalidation path.
It works on my machine and breaks on the build server. Help me work out what's different between the two.
The thing that notifies the other service is firing before we've actually saved the record. Swap the order.
Requests used to come back in under a tenth of a second and now take over a second. Figure out what changed.

Look over these changes and tell me whether two things could clear the stored copy at the same time and leave it wrong.
